description: Rules from spec/90-extensions/prov.md: the opt-in bridge that fixes how a record projects onto the W3C PROV family (PROV-1..PROV-6). Every vector names the bridge it exercises (CON-28), so an implementation that does not claim it skips them. PROV-4, PROV-5 and PROV-6 are consumer obligations and are exempted in exemptions.json. The claim has one member, so the vectors are the whole shape of the bridge: what is refused here is refused because PROV gives a document no identity and no hash to copy.

vectors.name: prov/claim-must-be-an-object
vectors.description: '2013' is the version, not the claim: a bare string leaves no room for the member the bridge may grow, and cannot be told apart from a value another extension might define under the same key.

vectors.name: prov/claim-must-not-be-null
vectors.description: JSON null is not an object and not an absent member: a record that writes the key with no claim is rejected, exactly as the schema types it.

vectors.name: prov/claim-must-not-be-an-array
vectors.description: An array of versions would be a claim about several editions, and PROV has one: the family recommended on 30 April 2013.

vectors.name: prov/version-is-required
vectors.description: A claim that names no edition cannot say which PROV family its projection follows, and an empty object is silence wearing the claim's clothes.

vectors.name: prov/version-must-be-the-covered-family
vectors.description: '2.0' is the version PROV does not have: the family was recommended once, on 30 April 2013, so a later-looking value names nothing.

vectors.name: prov/version-must-be-a-string
vectors.description: The number 2013 is not the string '2013': a version is a token, and a numeric one would sort by arithmetic in some consumers and not in others.

vectors.name: prov/claim-carries-no-document
vectors.description: PROV gives a document no required identity, so a 'document' member would be a URI the producer typed and nothing could resolve; 90.8 argues why the claim has one member.

vectors.name: prov/claim-carries-no-entity
vectors.description: 'ex:artifact-v2' is a PROV identifier, and no PROV identifier becomes the artifact's identity: the record's 'id' is the digest, and a second naming member would invite the reverse mapping 90.6 refuses.

vectors.name: prov/claim-carries-no-checksum
vectors.description: PROV reserves five attributes and none hashes bytes (§5.7.2), so a checksum in the claim could only duplicate the digest or carry a value with no subject.

vectors.name: prov/claim-with-version-only
vectors.description: The whole claim: one date. A record that carries nothing else is not claiming less than the bridge defines, because the bridge defines nothing else.

vectors.name: prov/claim-survives-a-full-projection
vectors.description: Every section the projection names may be present at once: lineage with a typed edge, a build recipe with a source and a toolchain, a state whose first transition is draft→candidate, and a producer. The claim requires no section and forbids none.

vectors.name: prov/a-record-without-the-claim-says-nothing
vectors.description: The scheme is literally named 'prov', and the record says nothing about PROV: a bridge that fired on a name rather than on a claim would make core conformance stricter than SCH-7 allows (ADR-0009). The one finding is the SCH-10 warning an unregistered name earns.
